patient.name: Hannah Kowalczyk
patient.complaint: Painless left neck lump for 2 months with night sweats
background: Weight 64 kg two months ago, now 57 kg
Works as a nursery teacher in Hackney

diagnosis.exam: Expect 'Which is the most likely diagnosis?' with a painless rubbery node: young adult with contiguous neck disease and alcohol pain (HL), older or HIV patient with widespread extranodal disease (NHL), or rapid mass with high phosphate (Burkitt's).

points: Hannah, 24, noticed a **lump in the left side of her neck** 2 months ago.
It does not hurt, and it is slowly getting bigger.
Drenching **night sweats**; she changes her T-shirt twice a night.
Odd thing: the lump **aches after a glass of wine**.

steps.lead: Hannah is a young adult with a lump in a lymph node: a lymphocyte malignancy, and at 24 **Hodgkin lymphoma** is the likelier type.

points: 3 cm **painless, rubbery, non-tender** left cervical node.
No axillary or groin nodes; no spleen or liver palpable.

steps.lead: Hannah's painless node with fever, sweats and weight loss is the lymphoma picture. Her **B symptoms** mean systemic disease and a poorer prognosis.

visual.title: Hannah's weight loss in 6 months
visual.label: Hannah 10.9%
visual.caption: 7 kg from 64 kg is just over 10% in 6 months: a B symptom, like her fever over 38°C and night sweats.

steps.lead: Neck node, orderly spread to the next group (supraclavicular) and **alcohol-induced pain**: Hodgkin lymphoma. Biopsy should show **Reed-Sternberg cells**.

steps.title: Hodgkin vs non-Hodgkin lymphoma
head: Feature
Hodgkin (HL)
Non-Hodgkin (NHL)
rows: No RS cells; atypical lymphoid cells

steps.lead: Hannah's node-to-node spread fits HL. **NHL** would be random and extranodal; **Burkitt's** is EBV-linked and grows explosively.

steps.q: Which feature of Hannah's history is classic (though uncommon) for Hodgkin lymphoma?
steps.r: **Alcohol-induced node pain** is classic HL. A painful tender node after a sore throat is reactive.

steps.lead: A young woman with mediastinal disease most likely has **nodular sclerosis** HL, the commonest subtype. Lymphocyte-depleted carries the worst prognosis.

steps.text: A tender node after a sore throat is reactive. Lymphoma nodes are **painless and rubbery**; be suspicious of any node above 2 cm lasting over 6 weeks.

investigation.exam: Expect 'diagnostic investigation' (excisional lymph node biopsy), staging imaging (PET-CT) and 'which stage?' using the diaphragm rule.

steps.q: Which test will confirm Hannah's diagnosis?
steps.r: **Excisional node biopsy** keeps the node architecture so the pathologist can classify the lymphoma. FNA is not enough.

steps.lead: Hannah has the whole left cervical node removed. It shows **Reed-Sternberg cells** in an inflammatory background: classic Hodgkin lymphoma.

steps.title: Hannah's bloods
steps.text: Mild anaemia, raised ESR and LDH; the film shows no abnormal cells.

steps.lead: Hannah's FBC and film are supportive, not diagnostic; a **CT** maps her disease.

visual.title: Hannah's chest X-ray
visual.caption: Widened mediastinum and enlarged hilar nodes: bulky mediastinal disease, typical of nodular sclerosis HL.

steps.lead: Hannah's **PET-CT** shows neck and mediastinal nodes, all **above the diaphragm**, with B symptoms: **stage IIB**.

visual.title: Lugano stage
bands: II: 2+ groups, one side of diaphragm
visual.label: Hannah IIB
visual.caption: Add A (no symptoms) or B (B symptoms), S for spleen, E for contiguous extranodal spread.

steps.text: The diaphragm is the dividing line: same side = **stage II**, both sides = **stage III**, liver, lung or marrow = **stage IV**.

management.exam: Expect hepatitis B screening before rituximab, IV fluids and rasburicase for Burkitt's, and neutropenic sepsis on chemotherapy.

steps.q: Hannah has stage IIB classical Hodgkin lymphoma. Which is most appropriate?
steps.r: Symptomatic stage IIB HL needs **chemotherapy** (e.g. ABVD), often with radiotherapy. Rituximab is for B-cell NHL.

steps.lead: Hannah's plan comes after staging: **chemotherapy** with or without radiotherapy. An older man with NHL would get **rituximab** with chemo, after **hepatitis B** screening.
Hannah's treatment is set by her **Lugano** stage, so accurate PET-CT staging comes before any chemotherapy.

steps.title: Before and during chemotherapy
nodes: Screen hepatitis B (and HIV) before rituximab
Fever on chemo: treat as neutropenic sepsis

points: Day 10 after her second cycle: **38.5°C**, shivering.

steps.lead: Hannah's fever with neutropenia is **neutropenic sepsis**: IV antibiotics within the hour. A **Burkitt** patient would also need IV fluids and **rasburicase**.
Hannah is monitored for **infection, marrow suppression** and organ damage from disease or treatment (e.g. bleomycin lung, anthracycline heart).

visual.title: Hannah's mediastinal node size
visual.caption: Interim PET after cycle 2 already shows a good response.

steps.text: Never start **rituximab** without checking **hepatitis B**: it can reactivate fatally.

science.exam: Expect mechanisms: rituximab targets CD20, B symptoms from IL-6/TNF-alpha, MYC in Burkitt's, contiguous vs non-contiguous spread.

steps.lead: Hannah's Reed-Sternberg cells came from **germinal centre B cells** that escaped apoptosis; with the inflammatory infiltrate around them they are diagnostic of HL.
Hannah's disease marched node to node (neck, supraclavicular, mediastinum) because HL spreads **directly through lymphatics**.

steps.title: Why Hannah sweats and loses weight
nodes: Tumour and immune cells release cytokines
Hypothalamus resets temperature: fever and sweats

steps.lead: Hannah's fever, sweats and weight loss are driven by **IL-6 and TNF-alpha**, which is why B symptoms reflect systemic disease.

steps.q: Why do patients with Burkitt's lymphoma need rasburicase?
o: Rapid cell turnover risks tumour lysis
steps.r: **MYC**-driven Burkitt's divides so fast that chemotherapy releases huge amounts of urate: **rasburicase** breaks it down.

steps.lead: Hannah's HL is slow by comparison. **Burkitt's MYC translocation** drives explosive growth and **tumour lysis**, so rasburicase is given.
Rituximab binds **CD20** on B cells; most NHL is B-cell, which is why it is added to chemo in NHL.

steps.text: Burkitt's: **MYC t(8;14)**, EBV, 'starry sky' histology, jaw or abdominal mass, and the highest TLS risk.

glossary.Lymphoma: Cancer of lymphocytes arising in lymph nodes or other lymphatic tissue.
glossary.Hodgkin lymphoma: Lymphoma with Reed-Sternberg cells, often in young adults, spreading node to node.
glossary.Non-Hodgkin lymphoma: Lymphomas without Reed-Sternberg cells; older adults, random and extranodal spread.
glossary.Reed-Sternberg cells: Large cells with bilobed nuclei and prominent eosinophilic nucleoli; diagnostic of Hodgkin lymphoma.
glossary.B symptoms: Fever above 38°C, drenching night sweats and weight loss over 10% in 6 months.
glossary.Cervical lymphadenopathy: Enlarged lymph nodes in the neck.
glossary.Contiguous: Spreading to the next adjacent node group in order.
glossary.Extranodal: Outside the lymph nodes, e.g. gut, bone marrow or skin.
glossary.Nodular sclerosis: Commonest Hodgkin subtype; young adults, often with mediastinal disease.
glossary.Lymphocyte-predominant: Hodgkin subtype with the best prognosis, often found early.
glossary.Mixed cellularity: Hodgkin subtype with intermediate prognosis, more common in older adults.
glossary.Lymphocyte-depleted: Rarest Hodgkin subtype with the worst prognosis; older or HIV patients.
glossary.Burkitt's lymphoma: Very aggressive EBV-associated B-cell NHL driven by MYC; high tumour lysis risk.
glossary.Anaplastic large cell lymphoma: T-cell NHL that can be aggressive with extranodal disease.
glossary.EBV: Epstein-Barr virus: causes glandular fever and is linked to Burkitt's and Hodgkin lymphoma.
glossary.MYC: Oncogene driving cell division; translocated in Burkitt's lymphoma.
glossary.Excisional lymph node biopsy: Surgical removal of a whole node for histology; gold standard for lymphoma.
glossary.Fine needle aspiration: Needle sample of cells; loses node architecture, so cannot classify lymphoma.
glossary.PET-CT: Scan combining metabolic activity with anatomy; used to stage lymphoma and assess response.
glossary.Lugano staging: Lymphoma staging system (stages 1 to 4) based on the diaphragm and organ spread; replaced Ann Arbor.
glossary.Ann Arbor: Older name for the lymphoma staging system now updated as Lugano.
glossary.Mediastinum: Central chest compartment between the lungs containing heart, great vessels and lymph nodes.
glossary.Rituximab: Anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody that kills B cells; used with chemotherapy in B-cell NHL.
glossary.CD20: Surface protein on B cells targeted by rituximab.
glossary.ADCC: Antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity: immune cells kill antibody-coated cells.
glossary.Hepatitis B reactivation: Flare of dormant hepatitis B when the immune system is suppressed, e.g. by rituximab.
glossary.Tumour lysis syndrome: Rapid cancer cell death releasing potassium, phosphate and urate with low calcium; risks AKI and arrhythmia.
glossary.Rasburicase: Recombinant urate oxidase that breaks down uric acid; prevents tumour lysis kidney injury.
glossary.Hyperphosphataemia: High blood phosphate, e.g. from rapid tumour cell breakdown.
glossary.Neutropenic sepsis: Fever or sepsis with neutrophils at or below 0.5; needs IV antibiotics within 1 hour.
glossary.IL-6: Interleukin-6: cytokine causing fever and acute-phase response; drives B symptoms.
glossary.TNF-alpha: Tumour necrosis factor alpha: cytokine causing fever and weight loss.
glossary.Germinal centre: Part of a lymph node follicle where B cells mature; origin of Reed-Sternberg cells.
glossary.ABVD: Standard Hodgkin chemotherapy: doxorubicin, bleomycin, vinblastine, dacarbazine.
glossary.LDH: Lactate dehydrogenase: raised with high cell turnover; a marker of lymphoma burden.
glossary.Starry sky: Biopsy appearance of Burkitt's: pale macrophages scattered among dark tumour cells.

technique.stem: A 22 year old man has a 6 week history of a painless swelling in the right side of his neck. He has had night sweats and has lost 6 kg. He notices the swelling aches after drinking alcohol. There is a 3 cm rubbery, non-tender right cervical lymph node. His temperature is 38.1°C.
technique.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?

steps.x: Diagnosis of a neck lump.
Young adult, painless rubbery node, B symptoms, alcohol-induced pain.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Hodgkin lymphoma**.

elim: Smooth, fluctuant, no B symptoms.
Tender nodes, sore throat; no alcohol pain.
Older adults; random, extranodal spread.
Possible with sweats, but alcohol pain and age favour HL.

steps.x: **B. Hodgkin lymphoma.** Rule: young adult + painless neck node + B symptoms + alcohol pain = HL.

technique.stem: A 31 year old woman has classical Hodgkin lymphoma confirmed on excisional lymph node biopsy of a cervical node. She has night sweats. She now needs her disease staged before treatment.
technique.q: Which is the most appropriate investigation?
o: Fine needle aspiration of other nodes

steps.x: Staging, not diagnosis.

clues: confirmed on excisional lymph node biopsy
steps.x: Confirmed HL needs whole-body staging.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **PET-CT**, used with the Lugano system.

elim: No longer routine for staging HL when PET-CT is available.
Misses abdominal and pelvic disease.
Diagnosis is already made; FNA does not stage.
CNS spread is not typical in HL.

steps.x: **E. PET-CT.** Rule: diagnose with excisional biopsy, stage with PET-CT.

technique.q: Which is the most appropriate management?

steps.x: Management after staging.

clues: night sweats and weight loss of 12%
steps.x: Stage IIB: two groups above the diaphragm, B symptoms.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Combination chemotherapy** (e.g. ABVD), ± radiotherapy.

elim: For CML.
For some B-cell NHL, not classical HL.
Lymphoma is not treated surgically.
She has symptomatic stage IIB disease.

steps.x: **A. Combination chemotherapy.** Rule: treatment is chosen after staging; symptomatic HL = chemotherapy.

technique.stem: A 34 year old man with Hodgkin lymphoma has a fever of 38.4°C most evenings, drenching night sweats and weight loss of 9 kg. Blood and urine cultures are negative.
technique.q: Which is the most likely mechanism of his symptoms?
o: Cytokine release such as IL-6 and TNF-alpha

steps.x: Mechanism of B symptoms.
Fever, sweats, weight loss with no infection.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Cytokines (IL-6, TNF-alpha)** from tumour and immune cells.

elim: Cultures are negative; these are B symptoms.
Causes thirst and confusion, not fevers and sweats.
No thyroid features.

practice.stem: A 28 year old woman has a 2 month history of a painless lump above her left clavicle and a dry cough. She has had drenching night sweats. There is a 4 cm rubbery, non-tender left supraclavicular node. Her temperature is 38.3°C, pulse rate 94 bpm and BP 112/70 mmHg. Chest X-ray shows a widened mediastinum.

visual.title: Chest X-ray
visual.caption: Widened mediastinum with enlarged hilar nodes.

practice.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
practice.e: A young adult with a painless rubbery node, B symptoms and a mediastinal mass has Hodgkin lymphoma. Sarcoidosis gives bilateral hilar nodes but not this node.

steps.x: Diagnosis of a node with mediastinal mass.
Young adult, painless rubbery node, B symptoms, mediastinal disease.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Hodgkin lymphoma** (likely nodular sclerosis).

elim: Tender nodes, sore throat; no mediastinal mass.
Bilateral hilar nodes and erythema nodosum; not a rubbery supraclavicular node with B symptoms.
Smokers in their 60s.
Anterior mediastinal mass without nodal disease and B symptoms.

steps.x: **A. Hodgkin lymphoma.** Rule: young adult + painless node + mediastinal mass + B symptoms = HL.

practice.stem: A 66 year old man has 3 months of tiredness and weight loss. He has painless lymph nodes in the left axilla and right groin, with none in between, and a mass in the stomach wall on CT. His temperature is 37.4°C, pulse rate 84 bpm and BP 136/82 mmHg.
practice.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
practice.e: NHL affects older adults and spreads non-contiguously with extranodal disease such as the GI tract. HL spreads node to node.

steps.x: Diagnosis from the pattern of spread.
Older man, non-contiguous nodes, extranodal GI involvement.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Non-Hodgkin lymphoma**.

elim: Lymphocytosis on FBC; gastric masses are unusual.
Would not explain scattered painless nodes.
Spreads contiguously; extranodal disease is uncommon.
Hilar nodes, younger, granulomas.

steps.x: **D. Non-Hodgkin lymphoma.** Rule: older + random spread + extranodal = NHL.

practice.stem: A 12 year old boy has a rapidly enlarging abdominal mass over 3 weeks. He has had glandular fever. Biopsy shows a 'starry sky' appearance.
practice.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
practice.e: Burkitt's lymphoma is EBV-associated, MYC-driven and grows very fast, with a starry sky appearance and high phosphate from cell turnover.

steps.x: Diagnosis of a fast-growing mass.
Explosive growth, EBV, starry sky, high phosphate and urate.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Burkitt's lymphoma**.

elim: Slow-growing, neck nodes, Reed-Sternberg cells.
Under 5s, renal mass, no starry sky.
Under 5s, catecholamines; no starry sky.
Indolent, older adults.

steps.x: **A. Burkitt's lymphoma.** Rule: rapid mass + EBV + starry sky + hyperphosphataemia = Burkitt's.

practice.stem: A 23 year old woman has a painless neck node and a large anterior mediastinal mass. Excisional biopsy shows Reed-Sternberg cells with bands of fibrous tissue dividing the node into nodules.
practice.q: Which is the most likely subtype?
practice.e: Nodular sclerosis is the commonest HL subtype, typical in young adults with mediastinal disease and fibrous bands in the node.

steps.x: Subtype from histology and presentation.

clues: fibrous tissue dividing the node into nodules
steps.x: Young woman, mediastinal disease, fibrous bands forming nodules.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Nodular sclerosis**.

elim: NHL, starry sky, no Reed-Sternberg cells.
Rare, older or HIV patients, advanced disease.
Usually localised peripheral nodes, not mediastinal.
More common in older adults.

steps.x: **E. Nodular sclerosis.** Rule: commonest HL = nodular sclerosis, young adults, mediastinum.

practice.stem: A 30 year old man is diagnosed with Hodgkin lymphoma after a painless, rubbery cervical node was excised. The node used to ache after alcohol. He has also had drenching night sweats for a month. His pulse rate is 82 bpm and BP 124/78 mmHg.
practice.q: Which feature of his history indicates a poorer prognosis?
practice.e: B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss) indicate systemic disease and a poorer prognosis. Alcohol pain is diagnostic, not prognostic.

steps.x: Which feature is a B symptom?
B symptoms mean systemic disease and a worse prognosis.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Drenching night sweats** (a B symptom).

elim: The commonest site; not adverse in itself.
Classic HL clue, not a B symptom.
Typical of lymphoma, not prognostic.
Typical of lymphoma, not prognostic.

steps.x: **B. Drenching night sweats.** Rule: B symptoms = fever >38°C, night sweats, weight loss >10%.

practice.stem: A 15 year old boy with Burkitt's lymphoma started chemotherapy yesterday. He now has muscle cramps and has passed little urine. His pulse rate is 112 bpm and irregular, and BP 104/62 mmHg.
practice.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
practice.e: Burkitt's lymphoma's rapid turnover makes tumour lysis syndrome likely after chemotherapy: high potassium, phosphate and urate with low calcium and AKI.

steps.x: Diagnosis after chemotherapy.
Burkitt's, day 1 of chemo, high K, phosphate, urate, low Ca, AKI.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Tumour lysis syndrome**.

elim: Calcium is low.
No fever; too early for the nadir.
Does not explain high phosphate and urate.
Causes hyponatraemia, not these electrolytes.

steps.x: **E. Tumour lysis syndrome.** Rule: Burkitt's + chemo + high K/PO4/urate + low Ca = TLS.

practice.stem: A 35 year old man has a 3 cm painless rubbery node in his left neck that has been present for 8 weeks. He has night sweats. His FBC is normal. An ultrasound confirms an abnormal lymph node.
practice.q: Which is the most appropriate diagnostic investigation?
practice.e: Excisional lymph node biopsy is gold standard because the architecture is needed to classify lymphoma; FNA is not enough.

steps.x: **C. Excisional lymph node biopsy.** Rule: lymphoma needs the whole node, not a needle.

practice.stem: A 40 year old woman has Hodgkin lymphoma. PET-CT shows involved nodes in the neck, axilla and mediastinum, and in the para-aortic region below the diaphragm. There is no organ involvement. She has no fevers, sweats or weight loss.
practice.q: Which is the most likely stage?
practice.e: Nodes on both sides of the diaphragm without organ disease is stage III; no B symptoms makes it A.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Stage IIIA**.

elim: Disease is on both sides of the diaphragm.
Both sides of diaphragm, and she has no B symptoms.
She has no B symptoms.

steps.x: **C. Stage IIIA.** Rule: both sides of diaphragm = III; no B symptoms = A.

practice.stem: A 64 year old man has diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. He is due to start rituximab with chemotherapy. His pulse rate is 78 bpm and BP 134/80 mmHg.

practice.stem: A 13 year old boy is diagnosed with Burkitt's lymphoma and is about to start chemotherapy. His urate is 0.49 mmol/L (0.12–0.36) and phosphate 1.9 mmol/L (0.8–1.5).
practice.q: Which is the most appropriate management to start with chemotherapy?
practice.e: Burkitt's has the highest tumour lysis risk; IV fluids and IV rasburicase prevent urate nephropathy and AKI.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

practice.stem: A 58 year old woman is receiving chemotherapy for non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Nine days after her last cycle she develops a fever and shivers. Her temperature is 38.6°C, pulse rate 116 bpm, BP 94/60 mmHg, respiratory rate 22 breaths per minute and oxygen saturation 96% breathing air.

steps.x: **C. IV piperacillin-tazobactam within 1 hour.** Rule: lymphoma + fever + neutropenia = neutropenic sepsis; antibiotics within an hour.

practice.stem: A 70 year old man with follicular B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma is treated with rituximab and chemotherapy. His lymph nodes shrink.
